# Why Website Styling Matters

A portfolio website should communicate information clearly while also
presenting a consistent professional identity. CSS controls the visual
appearance of HTML pages, while SCSS extends CSS with features such as
variables and organized style sections.

# CSS and SCSS Applications

CSS and SCSS can customize:

- Website colors and typography
- Navigation bars
- Headings and hyperlinks
- Images and cards
- Page spacing
- Dashboard elements
- Mobile responsiveness

# CSS versus SCSS

CSS contains the final styling rules used by a browser. SCSS makes those
rules easier to manage by supporting variables and reusable formatting.

For example, a color can be defined once and reused throughout a website:

```scss
$primary-color: #1f4e79;

h1,
h2 {
  color: $primary-color;
}
```

If the value of `$primary-color` changes, every rule using that variable
changes with it.

# Benefits for an Analytics Portfolio

Custom styling helps visitors understand the organization of a report.
Consistent colors distinguish headings, cards can emphasize findings,
and readable typography makes dashboards and research results easier
to interpret.

For a customer-insights portfolio, visual consistency also makes the
website appear more credible and professional.
